Hi there, Voat friends! This post aims to serve as an introduction to the Computer Guru Show for new listeners who find us here on Voat. If you have any questions about our show or how it's produced, please feel free to post them here.

The Computer Guru Show is a weekly radio show which aims to make technology accessible for everyone. When we say radio show, we're not just using that as a gimmick. Our show really is broadcast via terrestrial radio every week in Southern Arizona, and we reach over 80,000 listeners every Saturday. Although we have just recently started posting our content online, the Computer Guru Show has actually existed as a radio program for over 8 years.

The host of our show is Mike Swanson. Mike is the owner of [Arizona Computer Guru](http://azcomputerguru.com/), a Tucson-local computer repair, business IT, and website development service which has served the community for over 15 years. Mike is the Computer Guru, and not just in name. He's an expert in virtually all forms of IT, and heads our Business IT department in addition to owning and operating the company as a whole.

The show is co-hosted by Tara, who also operates a blog called [My Geek Obsession](http://mygeekobsession.com/). Rob is another frequent co-host of the show, and is the head of the website department at Arizona Computer Guru.

Every week on the show, we discuss interesting, funny, and important news in technology. Our goal is to help our listeners stay informed about the world of technology while also entertaining them in the process. In addition to discussing news, we take live calls from listeners who are often having issues with their computers or devices, and Mike troubleshoots those problems live on air. If a problem cannot be answered live due to time constraints or because the problem requires more research, we contact the listener after the show ends and offer them the same free tech support.

The reason we're posting our content online now is simple. We want to reach a wider audience and do more with the show than is currently possible. We have a lot of great ideas for the show, but we need a bigger online audience to make those things happen. Our main goal at the moment is to grow our online audience to the point where we can launch a longer format, internet-only supplement to the show. This extra edition of the Computer Guru Show would allow us to delve much deeper into the topics we discuss, as well as discuss things we wouldn't be able to talk about on the radio for a variety of reasons.

You can help make this possible in many ways, from something as simple as subscribing to our [YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCm0Q-NKIEHIxAqWqR1of4NQ), to sharing our show with your friends. If you *really* like the show, you can even support us on [Patreon](http://patreon.com/gurushow), though this is of course not required.

We hope you enjoy the show, and we look forward to seeing you around our community!
